PullRequest.Title: sessions: Add onboarding to the parallel work banner handoff
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Introduce the Agents Window when users click **Open Agents Window** from the parallel-work banner on a new-session screen.

- Preserve the draft handoff and pass the running session separately, so it can be revealed without opening it over the composer.
- Spotlight that session in the sessions list, then always continue with the V2 **workspaceAndModel** flow (workspace → model). Regular V2 variation selection is unchanged.
- Share the existing new-session onboarding seen state, respect disabled onboarding/AI features, and prevent automatic startup tours from racing the handoff.
- Temporarily reveal sessions hidden by filters, collapsed sections, or presentation caps; release the reveal when the tour ends without changing saved filters.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed
- 211 focused Electron unit tests — passed (banner ownership/draft handoff, tour sequencing and shared seen state, session-list reveals, and keyboard dismissal/focus restoration)
- ESLint on changed TypeScript files — passed
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed

Scenarios.Scenario: Clicking the parallel-work banner opens the Agents window, restores the draft, and schedules the running-session onboarding tour.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing nativeHostService.openAgentsWindow call and Electron window creation remain the user-visible open path. The new onboarding orchestration starts in the destination renderer after the handoff message; handleSelectAgentsFolder does not await it, and the draft/composer handoff completes before session resolution and tour presentation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the existing native host openAgentsWindow channel from the source renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one invocation per accepted banner click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same banner action already invoked openAgentsWindow once; the diff only adds one small URI component to its options.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This remains on the window-open critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create or reuse the Agents Electron browser window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One window open/reuse operation per accepted banner click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same ensureAgentsWindow/open path ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Window readiness gates delivery of the handoff message, as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send vscode:selectAgentsFolder to the opened renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One message per opened/reused Agents window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One message with the existing arguments was already sent; the diff appends one bounded URI payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Carries the draft/workspace handoff; the added session URI is serialized in the existing message and does not add a round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive asynchronously listed sessions from existing session providers/RPC and observe provider change events until the selected running session is present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No new provider request is initiated; in-memory lookup runs once initially and once per existing session-change event until success/cancellation/timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider session listing already occurred during Agents startup; the diff adds an event-driven consumer of that result for onboarding.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The tour waits for availability, but the composer handoff has already completed and the receiver does not await the onboarding promise.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the shared onboarding seen/outcome state through the existing Memento/storage service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded state updates for one first-run tour; none after the shared seen key is set.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This banner handoff did not run an onboarding scenario or persist its shown outcome.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs as part of tour presentation/outcome handling, after the new-session composer is available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One captured running-session URI and one draft per banner click. Session availability checks scan the providers' merged in-memory session collection on initial lookup and on provider change events until the target appears or the 15-second timeout expires; effective cardinality is total loaded sessions, but this is a one-time user action rather than a recurring render/input loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One handoff is active per SelectAgentsFolderContribution. Replacing _openIntent cancels the prior token, and ParallelWorkOnboarding's MutableDisposable disposes any prior pending store. OnboardingScenarioService serializes presentations and deduplicates the same scenario ID.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm behavior finds the session immediately in the provider-backed in-memory model. Cold behavior waits on existing provider change events; it does not issue a new provider request or poll repeatedly. Shown state is shared through the existing onboarding seen-key persistence, so completed/skipped tours do not repeat.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the IPC/window path, asynchronous non-awaited orchestration, provider lookup implementation, cancellation ownership, and shared seen-key behavior are directly visible in the changed and surrounding code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact provider session counts and cold provider-list latency vary, but the changed wait is off the composer critical path, event-driven, cancellable, and bounded to first-run onboarding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff does not add a boundary round trip to window opening, and deferred onboarding work is bounded, cancellable, and non-repeating after successful presentation.

Scenarios.Scenario: The first parallel-work tour opens the Sessions view, temporarily reveals a filtered/capped row, spotlights it, and releases the reveal.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the handoff and LifecyclePhase.Eventually, the onboarding presentation awaits openView and a synchronous SessionsList update/reveal before displaying the first spotlight. This work is on the tour's critical path but not on initial composer availability.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Each acquire and final release performs one full SessionsList.update over all loaded sessions, including filtering/grouping/sorting and tree reconciliation; effective cost is O(N log N) where sorting applies. The two rebuilds happen only for the one-time onboarding tour, not per frame, scroll, or session event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: OnboardingScenarioService presents scenarios serially. ParallelWorkOnboarding owns one DisposableStore, replacing/cancelling a previous handoff, while revealOnboardingTarget uses identity checks so disposal of an older reveal cannot clear a replacement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The list uses the already-loaded session model and existing tree virtualization/presentation caps. The targeted row bypasses filters/caps temporarily; no new external fetch or cache is created. The onboarding seen key prevents future completed/skipped runs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: reveal acquisition/release, complete list rebuilding, target registration disposal, list caps, and tour serialization are explicit in SessionsList and ParallelWorkOnboarding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large session histories can make each list rebuild noticeable, but there are only two bounded rebuilds for a one-time explicit onboarding flow and no evidence that they exceed existing accepted reveal behavior used by archive onboarding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The synchronous list work is bounded to two updates in a one-time user-triggered tour, preserves virtualization/caps except for one target, and cleans up target/disposable state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal Agents-window startup, banner eligibility updates, and ordinary session-list row rendering when no parallel-work onboarding is active.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SelectAgentsFolderContribution is a BlockStartup contribution and now constructs a lightweight ParallelWorkOnboarding coordinator. Its constructor only stores injected services and creates one MutableDisposable; it performs no list opening, provider lookup, DOM work, or external I/O until the special handoff runs.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Banner eligibility remains O(A) in loaded agent sessions, identical before and after for normal update events. Session render templates retain one observable autorun per rendered/virtualized row as before; the new DOM target registration executes only for the single active onboarding target.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing banner update events remain synchronous and coalesced by the contribution's _updating guard. The helper change from Array.some to Array.find preserves one short-circuit scan; the only additional scan is at the accepted click to capture the target URI.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or retained collection is added. _pending, target registrations, context keys, and reveal state are disposed/reset on completion, cancellation, replacement, or shutdown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor body, helper before/after behavior, row renderer lifecycle, and disposal ownership are directly established by the diff and surrounding implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: DI may instantiate services according to their existing singleton policy, but the added coordinator constructor itself has constant work and no boundary calls or subscriptions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup, steady-state CPU, or retention regression. The new eager object is lightweight, normal event-path scan complexity is unchanged, and target state has bounded cleanup.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 19 changed files and relevant call paths. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced; new work is confined to a first-run, user-triggered onboarding flow, remains off initial composer availability, reuses existing IPC/window/provider operations, performs bounded list rebuilds, and has explicit cancellation and cleanup.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
